$comment: The retry policy's parity table. The dashboard (ui/packages/app/lib/api/retry.ts) and the CLI (cli/src/lib/http-retry.ts) each replay every case through their own transport and must make the same number of attempts. A script entry is either an answer, `{ "status": N }` with an optional `retryAfterSeconds`, or a failure before an answer, `{ "error": CODE }` where CODE is a socket code Node's fetch puts on the error's cause, or `timeout` for the transport's own clock running out. Attempts beyond the script repeat its last entry. `preSendCodes` is the set of cause codes that prove a request never left; both classifiers assert their own set equals it. Both cap a `Retry-After` at `policy.retryAfterCapSeconds` and fail at once beyond it. A failure may also be `{ "error": "dropped" }`: the socket was lost after connecting. Bun reports that as a `TypeError` whose `code` is `ECONNRESET` on the error itself; Node reports the same event as `fetch failed` with `cause.code` `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, and both are their own rows. A transport failure that names a socket code is sent again whatever the method: a reply nobody saw is usually a request that never ran, and the operator re-running by hand would send it again anyway. `{ "error": "unsendable" }` is the exception — a `TypeError` with no code at all, the client refusing to send, which retrying cannot fix. `{ "error": "ERR_INVALID_URL" }` and `{ "error": "DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT" }` carry a code that is not about the connection but about the request itself, so neither lifts the replay gate: a write that failed either way is sent once. Reads still retry them, which this table does not pin — retrying a rejected certificate is a pre-existing waste, not something these rows govern.

cases.name: a read recovers from a blip
the ceiling holds against a backend that stays down
a refusal is final
a read obeys a rate limit
a read that timed out on the client is read again
a read reset after sending is read again
the replay-safe write is sent again after a gateway error
a write is not sent again after a gateway error
a write obeys a rate limit: the server did not run it
a write declined as a server timeout is sent again
a write that timed out on the client is sent once
a write refused at connect never left and is sent again
a write reset after sending is sent again
a write whose name did not resolve is sent again
a Retry-After beyond the cap fails at once, with the 429 in hand
a write dropped after sending is sent again
a write dropped after sending, as Node reports it, is sent again
a write stops at the ceiling when the socket keeps dropping
a write the client refused to send is sent once
a read dropped after sending is read again
a read dropped after sending, as Node reports it, is read again
a write the client could not address is sent once
a write refused over a certificate is sent once
